messages:
maria: FYI - customer (AcmeData) opened an escalation. They saw a spike in 5xxs and auth failures after what looks like a region failover. Their app suddenly routed to eu-west while they were pinned to us-west, and billing shows duplicate charge attempts. Repro steps from them below.

kevin: Can you paste the exact error payloads / trace ids? trying to correlate with proxy logs.

maria: Trace IDs: trace=acme-97f2, acme-97f3. Payloads show 401s with 'invalid_token' but only after the region flip. Their SDK logs: `ERROR Request failed: 401 invalid_token (region eu-west)`. They also saw repeated retries that look like billing double-counts.

jon: Looking at control-plane events around 2099991100-2099991145 — I see a routing policy roll we did for 'geo-fallback-sticky' at 2099991098 that included a small TTL change. Could be related.

deepa: I pulled probe heartbeats for the affected nodes: most probes were green but one health-check agent showed intermittent 200->500 for ~30s before the failover. Heartbeat log excerpt: `2026-03-16T17:12:31Z heartbeat=OK; 2026-03-16T17:13:02Z heartbeat=TIMEOUT; 2026-03-16T17:13:04Z health=DEGRADED`.

maria: Customer repro steps they sent (condensed):
1) long-lived connection from SDK to us-west, token created at 17:10.
2) at ~17:13 traffic flips to eu-west (no explicit error in SDK).
3) subsequent requests return 401 and client retries, causing two billable requests.
4) they reverted to pinned region and requests succeed.

kevin: Oof. So token validity is region-agnostic, but our auth proxy issues a per-region audience claim for some older tenants. If traffic goes cross-region it can be rejected.

jon: Agree. Hypothesis: heartbeat misfire caused smart-routing to trigger fallback to eu-west for a subset of connections. Because some legacy auth adapter asserts region claim, tokens rejected -> client retried -> duplicate billing.

deepa: Quick mitigation: flip routing policy to prefer 'pinned-region' for this customer and increase probe sampling for us-west agents. I can push a targeted override.

maria: Please do. Customer is asking for immediate mitigation + repro steps so they can audit billing.

jon: Action plan:
- deepa: apply targeted routing override for tenant acme-account to keep us-west only (rolling change, 1m).
- deepa: enable more frequent health checks on the us-west pool (sample rate x4) for 10m.
- jon: roll back the TTL tweak for geo-fallback-sticky, or at least revert it while we investigate.
- kevin: ask customer for full SDK logs + timestamps for the duplicated charge attempts.
- maria: open a billing incident to offer provisional credit if we confirm double billing.

deepa: On it. Pushing override now: `POST /control/v1/routing/overrides {"tenant":"acme-account","region":"us-west","reason":"heartbeat-misfire mitigation"}` -> response 200.

sre-bot: Deploy event: routing-overrides-service v3.14 deployed by deepa at 2099991190.

jon: Reverted TTL change in canary at 2099991198. No more canary traffic showing region flips for that policy.

kevin: Customer confirmed they can reproduce only when the routing flip happens. They attached SDK trace and billing timestamps. Forwarding to billing ops.

maria: Logging repro steps + artifacts to the customer case and starting a postmortem thread. Notes to include: heartbeat transient TIMEOUTs, recent TTL tweak to geo-fallback, legacy auth adapter that validates region claim, customer-observed retried requests causing duplicate billable events.

jon: Next investigative items: correlate probe agent logs with infra CPU/mem around 2099991125, and capture packet flows to see if NAT churn coincided. I'll also check if KV cache invalidation could make the auth adapter revalidate tokens.

deepa: Also adding a short-lived metric alert: if more than 1% of connections for pinned-tenants flip region in 1m => page eng-sre.

maria: Thanks all. I'll keep the customer updated and attach our mitigation steps. Will open a dedicated postmortem doc after we confirm root cause. :thumbsup:
